lesson.subtitle: Lesson 21 -- I Love My City
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Gabriela Pires | Lesson 21 -- I Love My City | Alumni by Better

listenings.text: Hi Gabriela, it's Ryan! I land in Sao Paulo on Friday morning, and I am so excited. I have never been to Brazil before, so I really need your help. My host family lives near a big avenue with a lot of traffic, and they told me the neighborhood is very crowded and a little noisy, but very safe. I want to see the real city, not only the famous places. Is there a good market near your house? I love street food, so a food truck would be perfect for me. And my sister told me there is amazing street art in Sao Paulo. Can you show me? One more thing: I do not have a car, so please choose places with a bike lane or a bus. See you on Friday!

Welcome to my city, Ryan. This is my favorite avenue, and there are museums, shops and cafes on both sides. On Sunday there are no cars here, so there is a huge bike lane for everyone. It is crowded and a little noisy, but I love it. Two blocks from here there is a small square with big trees. There are old buildings around it, and there is incredible street art on the walls. My grandmother goes to the market near the square every Saturday, and there is a food truck outside with the best sandwiches in Sao Paulo. At the end of the day we go up to a rooftop and we look at the city. There are lights everywhere. This is my city, and I love it.

extra_audio.text: First, you welcome your visitor and you say, welcome to my city. Next, you describe the street and you say, there is a big avenue near my house. After that, you say what is around and you say, there are shops and cafes on both sides. Then, you warn your visitor and you say, it is crowded and noisy, but it is safe. Finally, you invite your visitor and you say, let us go up to the rooftop and look at the city.
